title: Correlation between accretion rate and free-free emission in protoplanetary disks. A multiwavelength analysis of central mm/cm emission in transition disks
question: What is the nature of the central mm/cm emission close to the star in transition disks (thermal dust vs free-free from a jet or wind), and does it correlate with accretion, X-ray luminosity or mass-loss properties?

data.bands: Band 7 and 6 (1 mm), Band 4 and 3 (3 mm)

what.value: Centimeter flux densities of the targets (VLA/ATCA/GBT)

external_data.citation: Greaves & Mason 2022; Wright 2015; Casassus 2015; Rodriguez 2014; Zapata 2017; Osorio 2014; Macias 2017; Marino 2015; Ubach 2012

what.value: Stellar luminosities, accretion luminosities, accretion rates, X-ray luminosities (references 1-6)

evidence.quote: The last column reports the references for the luminosity, accretion luminosity, accretion rates, and X-ray luminosity.

external_data.citation: Vioque 2018; Wichittanakom 2020; Francis & van der Marel 2020; Manara 2023; Dionatos 2019; Ryspaeva 2023

evidence.quote: The inclination of the outer disks are from (cite: 2020FrancisAndVDMarel)

what.value: Class 0-I radio jet 3.6 cm luminosities for comparison

evidence.quote: fluxes of radio jets observed at 3.6 cm in a sample of younger Class 0-I disks ((cite: 2018Anglada))

what.value: TW Hya and LkCa 15 central-emission spectral indices and accretion rates

evidence.quote: (cite: 2021Macias) reported a the spectral index of the central emission of $\alpha_\text{inner}=0.65\pm0.05$

recipe.method: tclean on pipeline-calibrated data with per-image weighting chosen to maximize inner-disk S/N

recipe.goal: Measure inner and outer disk flux densities
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian imfit for inner flux; aperture photometry above 3 rms for total; outer = total minus inner; 5 rms upper limits
key_parameters: upper limit of 5 times the rms if no detection at 3 rms and cavity resolved

recipe.method: Linear fit of log F vs log nu; curve_fit if >2 points, else two-point; for GG Tau, HD100546, HD142527 extrapolate 1 mm dust to 3 mm and give interval [alpha_extrap, alpha_3mm-cm]
assumptions: 1 mm emission dominated by thermal dust for extrapolation

recipe.method: Optically thin blackbody dust mass formula using Band 6/7 flux, R_id upper limit = beam size
key_parameters: kappa = 10 cm2/g at 1000 GHz, beta = 1.0, flaring angle 0.02, R_subl = 0.07 sqrt(L*)

recipe.goal: Test free-free luminosity vs L_acc and L_X
recipe.method: Pearson correlation between free-free luminosity (from mm flux) and accretion/X-ray luminosity

recipe.goal: Compute ionized mass loss rate and correlate with accretion rate
recipe.method: Reynolds jet model equation; linmix regression of Mdot_i vs Mdot
key_parameters: T = 1e4 K, nu_m = 40 GHz, theta_min/theta_maj = 0.5, v_jet = 140 (M*/0.5 Msun)^0.5 km/s, jet inclination = outer disk inclination
assumptions: central emission is jet free-free emission

evidence.quote: The millimeter inner disk dust masses estimated in this way range between $0.004 M_\oplus$ and $1.37 M_\oplus$.

answer_key.quantity: Pearson r, free-free luminosity vs L_acc
Pearson r, free-free luminosity vs L_X
Power-law slope of Mdot_i vs Mdot

not_stated_but_needed: Which ALMA execution blocks/configurations were used for each project and spectral windows used for continuum
Mask, niter, threshold and cell/image size for tclean
Aperture radius used for total flux photometry
Fit function details for imfit (initial guesses, region)
Exact data used to compute the correlations (luminosity definitions for free-free luminosity and frequency)
Flux values for Table 1 SR24S etc. whether primary beam corrected
score_reason: Public data and clear recipe but many imaging details unstated and literature data needed.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, simple flux/spectral index analysis with numeric results.
